title: DirectChange: every price, in your currency
metaDescription: A free browser extension that shows the live equivalent of every foreign price, right next to it, in your own currency.
heroTitle: Every foreign price on the web, in your own currency, right next to it.
heroLede: DirectChange adds the live equivalent of every foreign price right after it, on any website. No more mental math, no more tab-switching to a converter.
metaFree: Free, open source, no account, no tracking.
metaBrowsers: Works in Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Brave, Arc and other Chromium browsers.
demoTitle: On any page, right where you look
demoLead: A trip wishlist in six currencies. Every price gets a small tag with its value in yours.
demoAlt: A trip wishlist with prices in yen, dollars, pounds, won, pesos and lira, each followed by its euro equivalent in a small orange tag
currLead: Yen, rupees, pesos or rand: DirectChange reads 150+ currencies and shows them in yours.
featTitle: Small, quiet, and right where you look
featLead: It does one thing: tell you what a price means to you, without leaving the page.
f1p: Near real-time rates for 150+ currencies, refreshed every 10 minutes. Hover any badge to see the exact rate and when it was fetched.
f2p: A “$” on a Canadian site is Canadian dollars. A “¥” on a Chinese site is yuan. DirectChange reads the domain, the page language, the shop's own data and the prices it shows.
f3p: ¥24,000, 1.234,56 €, MX$2,490, USD 45, 14 000 bahts, Rs 900… It even handles prices split across the page's HTML.
f4p: A small tag that adapts to light and dark pages. It's isolated from the site's styles, so it never breaks a layout.
f5p: Follows your browser by default, or pick a language in the settings. Right-to-left languages included.
f6p: No account, no analytics. The page is read on your device and never sent anywhere.
s1p: Add DirectChange to your browser. It takes ten seconds.
s2p: Euro, dollar, yen, rupee… any of 150+ currencies. It defaults to your region's currency.
s3p: Foreign prices get a small badge with their value in your currency, wherever you are on the web.
hoverAlt: Hovering a badge shows a card: 24,000 JPY, about €137, with the rate, time and source
convTitle: A converter that knows where you are
convLead: Setting a price filter on a foreign shop? Open DirectChange: it already knows the site's currency and has your budget converted into it.
c1s: It counts the prices on the page and picks the one the site really uses, even on a .com.
c2s: 1,000 € on a Japanese site? ≈ ¥175,700, before you even type.
c3s: Swap currencies in one click. Your last amount is kept for next time.
popupAlt: The popup on a Japanese site: a banner shows the site's currency, Japanese Yen, and the converter turns 1000 EUR into ¥175,638
langLead: This page follows your browser's language. Pick another one here or at the top of the page.
closeText: DirectChange collects nothing. The only requests it makes fetch exchange rates, and they say nothing about you or the pages you visit. The code is open source, so you can check.
madeBy: Made with care by Guillaume Gautier.
